question: ‘Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin’ was written by:
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Rammohan Roy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tuhfat-ul-Muwahhidin** (A Gift to Monotheists) was written by **Rammohan Roy**, one of the key figures in the Indian Renaissance.
 
• The book was written in the year **1804** and primarily aimed at advocating for **monotheism** (the belief in one God) and criticizing the superstitions associated with polytheistic practices.
 
• Rammohan Roy emphasized the need to return to the original teachings of religious texts, which were often distorted by later traditions and rituals.
 
• He is regarded as the **father of modern India** and a pioneer in introducing social, religious, and educational reforms during the 19th century.
 
• The work reflects his profound knowledge of **Islamic theology, Hindu scriptures, and Western philosophy**, which he used as tools to present his arguments.
 
• The book was written in **Persian**, the court language at that time, and included an introduction in **Arabic**, showcasing his linguistic versatility.
 
• Through this work, Rammohan Roy made a significant contribution to the movement against idol worship and the promotion of rationality in religion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sayyid Ahmed Khan**__

 __
 
• **Sayyid Ahmed Khan** was a prominent reformer and educationist who founded the **Aligarh Muslim University**.
 
• He worked to promote modern education among Muslims and is known for his role in the **Aligarh Movement**.
 
 
 
• **Akshay Kumar Dutt**__
 __
 
• **Akshay Kumar Dutt** was a rationalist and a social reformer associated with the **Brahmo Samaj**.
 
• He worked extensively on issues such as **caste discrimination, superstitions, and women's rights**.
 
 
 
• **Keshub Chandra Sen**__
 
 
• **Keshub Chandra Sen** was a leader of the Brahmo Samaj and played a significant role in **spreading its ideals**.
 
• He worked on issues such as **education for women, widow remarriage, and abolition of child marriage**.
